clue.text: Archbishop lang's world?

parts.note: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury from 1928 to 1942; his first name with a possessive attached reads as a word for the universe

explanation.surface: A question about the outlook or domain of a 20th-century Archbishop of Canterbury.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a pun on the first name of a 20th-century Archbishop of Canterbury, made possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmos is the universe seen as an ordered whole, the widest sense of world.

clue.text: Sweet's centre

definitions.meaning: a large round British hard-boiled mint sweet
the central ring of a dartboard or target

explanation.surface: A confectioner points to the middle of a sweet, or a sweet's soft middle.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a striped peppermint candy; the other is the innermost target ring that archers and darts players aim for.

clue.text: Star actor directing soldier

parts.note: to be leading is to be directing or guiding others
a man is a private soldier, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A film star who used to be in the army now gives orders on set.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal male performer in a play or film takes top billing as its star.

clue.text: Sharon and jo prepared to eat good Indian dish

indicators.note: to eat means the shuffled names take another letter inside them
prepared signals the names are worked up into a new arrangement, like ingredients

explanation.surface: Two friends named Sharon and Jo have cooked a decent curry to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' reads as a cook getting ready, but it is the anagram signal; 'to eat' is the container signal, so the good letter sits within the shuffled names.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogan josh is an aromatic lamb curry from Kashmiri cuisine, a staple of Indian restaurant menus.

clue.text: Shot in street, a bishop

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A news report of a clergyman being gunned down in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as a gunshot, but it is a noun meaning an attempt, as in have a shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A stab is an attempt or try at something, just as a shot is.

clue.text: Animosity beginning to tell in card game

parts.note: pique is resentment or ill feeling arising from wounded pride

indicators.note: beginning to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Ill feeling starts to show during a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Piquet is an old two-player trick-taking game played with a 32-card pack.

clue.text: Left university in ancient city in a depressed state

indicators.note: in means the abbreviations sit inside the name of the city

parts.note: Thebes was a great city of ancient Egypt, and another of ancient Greece

explanation.surface: A student who dropped out to live among ancient ruins is feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue is feeling sad, and the plural noun names a spell of melancholy.

clue.text: Ring the Parisian in boat being loaded

parts.note: a ring is round, so it gives the letter O

indicators.note: in means the French article goes inside the word for a boat

parts.note: a punt is a flat-bottomed river boat pushed along with a pole
le is French for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: Someone telephones a Frenchman whose boat is being filled with cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being loaded' reads as cargo going aboard, but it is slang for being rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for very wealthy, and opulent describes lavish riches.

clue.text: Catch some coming over

indicators.note: coming over in a down clue suggests turning the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: part means some, a portion of the whole

explanation.surface: Grab a few of them as they come across.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a device or trick to catch someone or something.

clue.text: Bird, variegated sort one's seen on church

indicators.note: variegated means marked with mixed colours, signalling the letters of sort are mixed up

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I; the 's stands for is, a link

explanation.surface: A colourful sort of bird has been spotted perched on a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variegated' rearranges sort into its first four letters; 'seen on' simply places one and church after them in an across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is the largest living bird, flightless and native to Africa.

clue.text: Play short tune, hit by abba initially

indicators.note: short means the word for a tune loses its final letter

parts.note: a melody is a tune
to ram is to hit or strike hard

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the word abba is used

explanation.surface: A brief song, a smash hit for the Swedish pop group Abba, introduces a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts MELODY to MELOD. 'hit by' reads as a pop chart hit, but it gives RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a sensational stage play with exaggerated characters and emotions.

clue.text: Confused impression given by book publisher's hype

parts.note: a blur is a vague or indistinct impression

explanation.surface: A muddled picture of a novel is created by its marketing copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurb is the short promotional description printed on a book's jacket.

clue.text: Good man presented with one German beer mug

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is a good man in crossword convention
ein is the German for one

explanation.surface: A virtuous fellow is handed a German tankard.
explanation.definitionFit: A stein is a large earthenware tankard of the type used for beer in German taverns.

clue.text: It's featured in W African fetish for unarmed combat

indicators.note: featured in means the first word sits inside the following word

parts.note: juju is a West African charm or fetish believed to hold magic power
it's taken as the letters it and s, with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A martial art is apparently involved in a West African fetish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featured in' is the container signal: the West African charm word opens after its third letter to take the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Jujitsu is a Japanese martial art of fighting without weapons using holds and throws.

clue.text: Happy chappie producing a flag

parts.note: jolly means cheerful or happy
Roger is just a man's name, standing for any chap

explanation.surface: A cheerful bloke turns out a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jolly Roger is the traditional pirate flag showing a skull and crossbones.

clue.text: Fruit that might go off?

definitions.meaning: a tropical fruit with spiky skin and sweet yellow flesh
military slang for a hand grenade, whose segmented casing resembles the fruit

explanation.surface: A fruit that could go rotten if left too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' suggests spoiling food, but here it means explode.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropical fruit's name is also soldiers' slang for a hand grenade, which explodes.

clue.text: A remake of timeless mountie film

indicators.note: a remake rebuilds an existing film, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A Canadian Mountie movie is being remade with no time period.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen letters of TIMELESS MOUNTIE rearrange into the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Meet Me in St. Louis is a 1944 MGM musical starring Judy Garland.

clue.text: Us singer encountered crossing a lounge

indicators.note: crossing means the word for encountered goes across and around the a

parts.note: met is the past tense of meet, meaning encountered
to loaf is to lounge about idly

explanation.surface: Someone ran into a famous singer who was crossing a hotel lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lounge' reads as a room but is the verb, giving LOAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat Loaf was the American rock singer known for the album Bat Out of Hell.

clue.text: Relatives, American, in the us itself

parts.note: uncles are relatives

explanation.surface: Relations who are American, living in the United States itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded figure in a top hat is the national personification of the US government.

clue.text: Musical instruction at an end, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests the words are in a sorry state, so their letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: It is all over, unfortunately.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a tempo marking telling players to go at a moderate walking pace.

clue.text: Energetic type wanting Monday off

indicators.note: off means the letters of Monday are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: A hard worker who would like a day off at the start of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a forceful, tireless person, named after the electrical generator.

clue.text: Child in river having capsized boat

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for child goes inside the river's name
having capsized means the river's name is overturned and reads backwards

parts.note: the Tay is the longest river in Scotland

explanation.surface: A child was in the river when the boat overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having capsized' turns the Scottish river backwards to YAT, and 'in' is the container signal; capsized boat is a red herring, as the river is what turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht is a sailing or motor vessel used for pleasure or racing.

clue.text: An Irish bay — bay, say, skirting a lake

indicators.note: skirting means going round the edge, so the word for a tree encloses the letters

parts.note: the bay laurel is an example of a tree, as say signals

explanation.surface: An Irish inlet, a bay as it happens, runs around the edge of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'bay' is not water but the bay laurel, a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Tralee Bay is an inlet of the Atlantic on the coast of County Kerry in Ireland.

clue.text: Put money on a Greek character

parts.note: to bet is to put money on something

explanation.surface: Gambling on a person from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Solitary type in cell one, reading

indicators.note: in means the answer is found inside the run of words cell one, reading

explanation.surface: A prisoner held alone in a cell is passing time with a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner is someone who prefers to be alone and avoids company.

clue.text: Artist, getting on, is seldom seen

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
re means on or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A painter in old age is hardly ever spotted any more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting on' reads as ageing, but 'getting' is a link and 'on' gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare is uncommon, so it is not often encountered.

clue.text: Remarkable things — father describes number collected by macho types

indicators.note: describes in the geometric sense of drawing around, so father goes round everything else

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: collected by means the abbreviation for number is held inside the macho types

parts.note: he-men are strong, aggressively masculine men

explanation.surface: A father tells of a number being gathered up by tough guys, which is remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describes' is used in the geometric sense of drawing a line round, and 'collected by' is a second container signal nested inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are extraordinary occurrences or marvels, the plural of phenomenon.

clue.text: Rodney, perhaps, might mean very well by dropping out

indicators.note: dropping out means the word by is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: admirably means very well, in a way deserving praise

explanation.surface: Rodney might be doing very well by leaving school early.
explanation.walkthrough: Rodney is the 18th-century British naval commander George Rodney, an example of the definition, as 'perhaps' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: George Rodney was a Royal Navy commander who beat the French at the Saintes in 1782, a naval officer of top rank.

clue.text: Typical of girl kept in a long time

indicators.note: kept in means the girl's name is held inside the word for a long time

parts.note: an age is a very long time
Vera is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Typical of a girl to be shut indoors for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Average means ordinary or normal, like the usual run of things.
